text:
Priya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing — a couple customers asked about how credit buckets behave during transient spikes. Who can confirm the canonical policy for bursts vs hard quota enforcement? Also: any planned changes to exemption rules for endpoints? @Alex

Alex: Short answer — we have per-account credit buckets + a small burst pool applied at the gateway for short spikes. We're evaluating whether to widen the burst window. Need finance + infra input before we change defaults.

Jamal: Current policy summary (quick): 1) baseline bucket refills hourly; 2) we apply a 5-minute burst buffer (10% of daily allowance) to smooth short spikes; 3) sustained overage triggers tiered throttling. We're proposing a tiered-burst pilot next quarter. cc @Maria for infra implications.

Maria: Infra note — burst is enforced in the gateway rate-limiter. Increasing window from 5m -> 15m requires: small state change in limiter, rollout gating, and extra e2e tests. Canary rollout (10% traffic) looks safe.

Priya: Thanks. Can someone draft a customer-facing blurb that explains "what to expect" and the process to request an exemption? Some customers asked for a concrete example of headers they see when approaching limits.

Sam: I'll draft the copy. A couple clarifications on exemptions: we only grant per-account exemptions for Enterprise customers via contract clause + usage review; Security needs to sign off for any long-lived exceptions. Ad-hoc exceptions are rare.

Maria: Also FYI: function-calls endpoints are weighted differently than embeddings in quota math — please call that out in the doc.

Jamal: Finance: if we widen the burst window without a commitment, estimated margin impact ~2-3% monthly. We should model scenarios tied to minimum commitments to offset cost.

Priya: :thumbsup: Please post the draft here. Also add a short example showing the rate-limit headers customers will see (copyable).

Maria: Example headers customers will get (gateway):
```
x-rw-credits-remaining: 3450
x-rw-burst-remaining: 300
x-rw-quota-reset: 1762349200
```

nodebot: All-hands recording uploaded — https://redwood.example.com/all-hands/1762345678 (transcript attached).

Alex: Follow-up action — Product to propose a self-serve exemption flow for Dedicated/Enterprise customers (console + ops review). Deliverable: specific UX + audit trail by EOW.

Lina: Quick question — do new signups still get a short grace from burst caps? We mentioned a protection window earlier.

Alex: We keep a 15-minute grace window for new signups to avoid immediate throttles. We'll add exact wording to the draft.

Priya: Great — I'll coordinate with Sam + Maria to get the customer-facing doc out and link the canary rollout plan. Thanks everyone.
